correctness.rationale: For each agent, the own-bundle sum is Gamma(r,1). The largest rival remainder after arbitrary single-good deletion is (r-1)M+Gamma(r-1,1), with M an independent Exp(r) minimum. The survivor CDF follows from a direct convolution and yields the stated exact rational finite expansion. Disjoint agent-good rows make all individual EFX-success indicators independent, giving Binomial(n,p). The rival survivor tail has leading term r t^(r-2)e^(-t)/(r-2)!, so Gumbel centering and a three-region dominated-convergence argument give p~log(n)/(r(r-1)n). Binomial concentration and CLT yield the count limits. Twenty exact-versus-independent-quadrature cases (r=2..5,n=2..6), the harmonic identity for r=2, and five direct-valuation Monte Carlo comparisons passed. The limit does not depend on these finite experiments. No independent validation was performed.

originality.rationale: The sharp EFX survival constant and the logarithmic binomial EFX-satisfaction law were not found in inspected directly relevant primary works or in targeted research-record searches. The nearest earlier fixed exponential-lottery calculation concerns EF1, which deletes a most-valuable rival good and studies a different sum of smallest values; neither its CDF nor its limit implies the EFX largest-remainder calculation. The papers about lotteries focus on exact EF, while online papers randomize the allocation under worst-case utilities. This is a provisional original-claim assessment, not a proof of uniqueness across all literature.
residual_risks: Relevant work on random EFX existence or counting could contain a special-case corollary not indexed by title or phrase; the targeted comparisons do not establish global priority.

value.rationale: EFX is a standard strong fairness requirement, and ex-post compliance of an ex-ante balanced allocation under independently uncertain values is a natural quantity of interest. The exact rational finite law and universal fixed-r decay constant sharpen qualitative impossibility results. A binomial logarithmic-satisfaction effect distinguishes individual success from system-wide success, making the exact invariant relevant without invoking an unrelated downstream theorem. It is not a table recomputation or a mere parameter substitution. The domain is deliberately stated so no claim is made for optimal adaptive allocations.
